# ACT_PHASE=C0-RED

# C0-P1: THE SOURCE INTERVAL AND DIGEST IDENTITY AUDIT.
# The committed source blob was read FROM GIT (not from the working
# tree) and every recorded interval was rehashed by TWO INDEPENDENT
# METHODS:
#   METHOD-A  POSIX  : dd if=<blob> bs=1 skip=<s> count=<n> | shasum -a 256
#   METHOD-B  Git    : git cat-file blob <oid> | tail -c +<s+1> | head -c <n> | shasum -a 256
# A third independent instrument (a self-contained C SHA-256 scanner,
# validated against the FIPS-180 "abc" vector AND against the
# sha256("hello world") vector) searched EVERY (start,length) pair
# over the whole file.
# THE SCANNER'S SELF-TEST IS MANDATORY AND WAS PERFORMED: the same
# scanner MUST find the three C1 digests at exactly the C1 offsets,
# and it DID:
#     MATCH w=0 start=35517 len=583 end=36100
#     MATCH w=1 start=36577 len=442 end=37019
#     MATCH w=2 start=37566 len=152 end=37718
# A scanner that found nothing would have been rejected as broken.
# The scanner's argument handling was itself found and fixed during
# this ACT (an initial run mis-parsed the window arguments and
# searched nothing); the corrected scanner was re-validated against
# the positive control above before the exhaustive run was trusted.
# THE INTERVAL CONVENTION WAS ESTABLISHED MECHANICALLY, NOT ASSUMED:
# the recorded digests are reproduced ONLY by the ZERO-BASED,
# HALF-OPEN convention [start, end) with length = end - start.
# The one-based-inclusive and zero-based-inclusive conventions were
# both tested and both FAIL.
# PART 1: THE C1 RECORD (evidence/.../RECON03/c1/core-sites.tsv)
# RESULT: ALL THREE C1 DIGESTS REPRODUCE EXACTLY under [start,end).
# VERDICT: PASS

column1: # PART 3: THE MECHANICALLY DETERMINED AUTHORITATIVE BOUNDARY TABLE
# Produced by the C scanner, NOT by reading the predecessor's claims.
# The scanner enumerated every (start,length) pair over the whole
# 101705-byte blob and reported the unique match for each digest.
# The scanner's self-test: it MUST and DID find the three C1 digests
# at exactly the C1 offsets. A scanner that found nothing would have
# been rejected as broken.
# FOR and INV: the C1 ranges do NOT cover the whole function. They
# stop at the end of the FLOAT switch. The integer switch, the other
# half of the decision table, lies OUTSIDE the recorded range. This is
# exactly the "body versus whole definition" distinction the ACT
# asked to be tested, and it is confirmed:
#   - C1 FOR range = the FLOAT SUB-TABLE ONLY (lines 864..877)
#   - C1 INV range = the FLOAT SUB-TABLE ONLY (lines 893..904)
#   - C1 CSET range = the WHOLE function (lines 921..923)
# so the three C1 ranges are NOT a consistent "function boundary"
# concept either. The C2 contract ranges ARE whole definitions (plus
# trailing newline), so C2 and C1 describe DIFFERENT byte sets while
# C2 REUSES C1's digests.

column1: # PART 5: THE CONCLUSION FOR C0-P1
# The ACT requires: "Accept only: one mechanically determined
# authoritative function-boundary table, its exact bytes/hash/OID and
# an independently demonstrated, already authorized mapping to the
# frozen contract."
# The mechanically determined table EXISTS and is recorded above
# (PART 3). The mapping to the frozen contract DOES NOT: the frozen
# contract's section 2 table states a RANGE and a DIGEST that are
# mutually inconsistent -- the named range does not hash to the named
# digest under any convention, and the digest belongs to a different
# byte set entirely.
# The ACT further requires: "If the binding frozen contract contains
# invalid source-range/hash claims requiring changed bytes, no hidden
# correction inside IMPLEMENT02: HALT_SOURCE_RANGE_DIGEST and propose
# a forward-only RECON03-contract correction."
# C0-P1 VERDICT = FAIL
# DISPOSITION = HALT_SOURCE_RANGE_DIGEST
# NOTE: this is NOT a label-only explanation. Part 3 shows the two
# concepts are genuinely different byte sets (583 vs 1059 bytes for
# FOR; 442 vs 918 for INV; 152 vs 153 for CSET), and the recorded
# digest demonstrably belongs to the C1 byte set. A label-only
# explanation would require the two byte sets to be equal, which they
# are not, and which the exhaustive whole-file search independently
# confirms cannot be equal for any interval pair.
